# `dump --stage checked` prints a match back as the match it is, so the dump
# checks again and prints the same: a statement, an expression, a headless
# match, an option's, and the last arm of an exhaustive match keeping its
# patterns.

sngl dump --stage checked app.sngl
cp stdout first.sngl
sngl check first.sngl
sngl dump --stage checked first.sngl
cp stdout second.sngl
cmp first.sngl second.sngl

grep 'match d \{ up, down => "vertical"; else => "horizontal" \}' first.sngl
grep 'match \{' first.sngl
grep 'match hand \{ left \{' first.sngl
grep 'null => "none"' first.sngl
grep 'left => Dir.up' first.sngl

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:test"
import . "sngl:ui"

enum Dir { up, down, left, right }

const hand = Dir.left

// Headless: a tagless switch in Go and a subjectless when in Kotlin.
// JavaScript has nothing to switch on and writes the if chain.
func grade(n int) string {
    match {
        n >= 90 { return "a" }
        n >= 50 { return "b" }
        else { return "c" }
    }
}

// A break in an arm leaves the loop around the match, which Go's and
// JavaScript's switch would take as their own: the if chain.
func firstDown(ds list[Dir]) int {
    var at = -1
    for var i, d = ds {
        match d {
            down {
                at = i
                break
            }
            else {}
        }
    }
    return at
}

// An option is compared as `==` compares one: the if chain.
func name(d option[Dir]) => match d {
    null => "none"
    up => "up"
    else => "other"
}

func turned(d Dir) => match d {
    up => Dir.right
    right => Dir.down
    down => Dir.left
    left => Dir.up
}

component pad node {
    var d Dir = up
    var maybe option[Dir] = null
    // An initializer holds no statement: a func literal called where it
    // stands in Go, a when in Kotlin.
    var axis = match d {
        up, down => "vertical"
        else => "horizontal"
    }
    // A lambda's body is a function's.
    var flips = [Dir.up, Dir.left].map(func(x Dir) => match x {
        up => Dir.down
        else => Dir.up
    })

    // A match on a constant is the arm it takes.
    match hand {
        left { text(value="left-handed") }
        else { text(value="unfolded") }
    }
    text(value=axis)
    text(value=name(maybe))
    text(value=grade(firstDown(flips) * 60))
    button #turn(text="Turn", @click {
        d = turned(d)
    })
}

func testHeadless(t Test) {
    t.assert(grade(95) == "a")
    t.assert(grade(60) == "b")
    t.assert(grade(10) == "c")
}

func testBreak(t Test) {
    t.assert(firstDown([Dir.up, Dir.down, Dir.down]) == 1)
    t.assert(firstDown([Dir.up]) == -1)
}

func testOption(t Test) {
    t.assert(name(null) == "none")
    t.assert(name(Dir.up) == "up")
    t.assert(name(Dir.left) == "other")
}

func testComponent(t Test, c pad) {
    t.assert(c.axis == "vertical")
    t.assert(c.maybe == null)
    t.assert(c.flips[0] == Dir.down)
    c.turn.click()
    // A test's own match.
    match c.d {
        right { t.assert(true) }
        else { t.assert(false) }
    }
}

window {
    pad
}
